question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Chandernagore — Location & French Establishment]
options: Chandernagore is located on the banks of the Hooghly River in present-day West Bengal
Chandernagore was established as a French trading post in 1673 with permission from Ibrahim Khan, the Mughal Subahdar of Bengal
Chandernagore is situated on India's western coast, near the Gulf of Kachchh, to tap the cotton trade
The French built Fort d'Orléans at Chandernagore to defend their Bengal trading center
wrong_fact: Chandernagore is NOT on India's western coast near the Gulf of Kachchh. It is situated in eastern India, on the bank of the Hooghly River in Hooghly district, West Bengal, about 35 km north of Kolkata.
explanation: Chandernagore (Chandannagar) was established in 1673 by the French East India Company on the banks of the Hooghly River in Bengal. It became a prosperous trading center under Jean-Baptiste Chevalier and Dupleix, fortified by Fort d'Orléans. It has no geographical connection to Gujarat or the western coast of India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Chandernagore — Capture & Seven Years' War]
options: During the Seven Years' War, a British force under Robert Clive and Admiral Watson captured Chandernagore in March 1757
The capture of Chandernagore eliminated the French threat in Bengal prior to the Battle of Plassey
Chandernagore was located downstream of Calcutta, allowing the French to block British access to the Ganges river network
The French lost Fort d'Orléans when the British bombarded it from warships on the Hooghly River
wrong_fact: Chandernagore was NOT located downstream of Calcutta. It is located upstream (north) of Calcutta. This meant Calcutta lay between Chandernagore and the Bay of Bengal, so the British at Calcutta were the ones who could block French access to the sea, not vice versa.
explanation: Chandernagore lies upstream of Calcutta. In March 1757, during the Seven Years' War, Robert Clive and Admiral Charles Watson sailed up the Hooghly River and bombarded Chandernagore, destroying Fort d'Orléans. Capturing Chandernagore secured the British rear and neutralized French alliance prospects with Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah before the Battle of Plassey in June 1757.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Chandernagore — Post-Independence Merger & Geography]
options: In June 1949, the citizens of Chandernagore voted in a referendum to merge with the Indian Union
Chandernagore was the only French territory in India that was not a coastal enclave, being located inland in Bengal
Unlike other French enclaves like Pondicherry and Karaikal, Chandernagore was officially integrated into West Bengal state in 1954
Chandernagore was surrounded entirely by the Princely State of Cooch Behar, which delayed its integration into India
wrong_fact: Chandernagore was NOT surrounded by the Princely State of Cooch Behar. It was surrounded by the Hooghly district of West Bengal (formerly part of British Bengal Province). Cooch Behar is a princely state located in northern Bengal, hundreds of kilometers away from Chandernagore.
explanation: Chandernagore was a French enclave located inland along the Hooghly River, surrounded by Hooghly district. Following a referendum in June 1949 in which the population overwhelmingly voted to join India, the French transferred de facto control in 1950. The treaty of cession was signed in 1951, and it was integrated into West Bengal in 1954 (under the Chandernagore Assimilation of Laws Act). Cooch Behar is a separate region in north Bengal.
